title: Degree of quadratic-APN ortho-derivatives
summary: Prove that the ortho-derivative of every quadratic APN function has algebraic degree exactly two below the dimension.

formal_statement.body: Let $n\ge4$, let $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$ be quadratic and APN, and let $\pi_F$ be its unique ortho-derivative normalized by $\pi_F(0)=0$. Prove that $$\deg(\pi_F)=n-2$$ for every such $F$, or exhibit a valid counterexample. Under Gorodilova's componentwise formulation, this asks that every nonzero component $v\cdot\pi_F$ have degree $n-2$.

scope.domain: Quadratic APN functions and their ortho-derivatives
assumptions: $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$ is quadratic and APN
scope.unresolved_remainder: The 2024 public workshop paper proves the general upper bound $\deg(\pi_F)\le n-2$. A 2026 preprint claims the full componentwise equality conjecture, but peer-reviewed confirmation of that complete solution is not yet available.

provenance.note: The TIT paper explicitly attributes the conjecture to Gorodilova, and the public author manuscript arXiv:2005.10788 states the same componentwise claim as Conjecture 2.

progress.summary: The TIT source reports the experimentally observed degree $n-2$ and explicitly attributes the conjecture to Gorodilova.
A public workshop paper proves that every quadratic-APN ortho-derivative has algebraic degree at most $n-2$, without proving the required equality.
A preprint claims a proof that every nonzero component has degree $n-2$, which would resolve the conjecture, but the claim is not yet peer reviewed.
